samples.summary: Vacuous assertion: orientation/paper-size seeding is not actually verified
samples.evidence: The test 'seeds the margins from the document, converted to inches' passes a document with `paperSize: PAPER_SIZES.A4, orientation: 'landscape'` and asserts `expect(screen.getByLabelText('Landscape')).toBeTruthy()`. The Landscape radio item and its `<Label htmlFor="page-setup-landscape">` are rendered unconditionally by DocsPageSetupDialog (docs-page-setup-dialog.tsx, the RadioGroup always renders both items), so this assertion is true whether or not the seeding useEffect sets `orientation`. It never checks `aria-checked`/`data-state`, and there is no assertion anywhere that the paper-size Select shows 'A4'. Consequently nothing in the suite would fail if `setOrientation(current.orientation)` / `setPaperSize(current.paperSize)` were dropped or wrong — Apply would then silently rewrite a landscape/A4 document back to portrait Letter, a visible document change. The other dialog tests all start from LETTER_DEFAULT/portrait, so they cannot catch it either.
searchedFor: grep for aria-checked/data-state in the test and in components/ui/radio-group.tsx
grep for PAPER_SIZES.A4 assertions in the test

samples.summary: 'held format survives a paste' test never verifies the paste happened or that it can be applied twice
samples.evidence: The test titled 'the held format survives a paste, so one pick-up can be applied twice' calls `editor.pasteFormat()` without checking its return value or the resulting document, then only asserts `hasCopiedFormat()` is true. That assertion also holds if `pasteFormat()` did nothing at all (a no-op path also leaves the buffer set), and no second paste onto a different selection is ever performed, so the stated 'applied twice' behaviour is untested.

samples.summary: Read-only pasteFormat document assertion is vacuous (bold was never present)
samples.evidence: `para('b1', 'hello world')` builds inlines with `{ fontFamily: 'Arial', fontSize: 12 }` and no `bold` (editor-read-only.test.ts:83-90). The caret format copied from that block therefore contains no `bold` either, so `expect(...inlines.every(i => !i.style.bold)).toBe(true)` is true whether or not the read-only guard blocks the write. Only the `expect(editor.pasteFormat()).toBe(false)` line carries weight; the document check adds no coverage. A styled fixture (or asserting fontSize/other property that the copied format would change) would make it real.

samples.summary: Toolbar toggle's cancel-with-no-selection path is untested
samples.evidence: FormatPainterToggle documents 'With nothing selected the second press just lets it go, which is how the painter is cancelled.' In docs-format-painter-toggle.test.tsx the stub is `pasteFormat: vi.fn(() => held)` — it ignores selection entirely, so no test distinguishes the paint case from the cancel case; both press sequences look identical. The single-shot-vs-cancel semantics are asserted only through mock call counts.

samples.summary: No test that pasteFormat triggers notifyStyleApplied only when it wrote
samples.evidence: `EditorAPI.pasteFormat` conditionally calls `notifyStyleApplied()` (editor.ts, `if (applied) notifyStyleApplied();`) so toolbar pickers re-read their summaries. Neither editor-format-painter.test.ts nor the frontend tests subscribe to `onCursorMove`/style-applied to verify the notification fires on a successful paste, or that it does not fire on a no-op paste. A regression would leave toolbar state stale after painting.

samples.summary: The CUSTOM paper-size sentinel branch has no test
samples.evidence: The dialog renders a `Custom (name)` SelectItem when the document's paper size matches no preset, and picking it is deliberately a no-op. No test in docs-page-setup-dialog.test.tsx constructs an editor whose `getPageSetup()` returns an off-preset paper size, so neither the label nor the no-op behaviour is covered; a regression would silently relabel an imported document's paper size as 'Letter' and could apply Letter dimensions.

samples.summary: Mobile overflow 'Page setup' entry is untested
samples.evidence: The dialog is mounted at the toolbar root specifically because the mobile overflow DropdownMenu unmounts its children (comment at the pageSetupOpen state). The new toolbar test only exercises the desktop `aria-label="Page setup"` button; the matchMedia stub forces `matches: false`, so the mobile branch and the DropdownMenuItem that sets `pageSetupOpen` are never rendered or clicked in any test.

samples.summary: Export failure path (toast instead of unhandled rejection) is not tested
samples.evidence: docs-export-button.test.tsx header claims 'every entry has to reach the download through the same runExport path, so a failure raises a toast rather than an unhandled rejection', but no test makes an export action reject or asserts a toast.error. Only success paths for Markdown and text are covered.

verdict.reason: Verified in-repo. The test at docs-page-setup-dialog.test.tsx:59-73 is the only one seeding a non-default setup (A4/landscape), and its sole orientation assertion is `expect(screen.getByLabelText('Landscape')).toBeTruthy()` (line 72). In docs-page-setup-dialog.tsx:220-239 the RadioGroup renders both items and `<Label htmlFor="page-setup-landscape">Landscape</Label>` unconditionally, so that query resolves regardless of the `orientation` state — the assertion holds whether or not the seeding effect (lines 121-127) sets orientation. No test asserts aria-checked/data-state, and a repo-wide grep found no assertion on the paper-size Select (SelectValue, line 197) showing 'A4'. The gap is not covered elsewhere: DEFAULT_PAGE_SETUP is LETTER/portrait/96px (packages/docs/src/model/types.ts:745-749), identical to the initial useState (lines 111-119) and to LETTER_DEFAULT (test lines 39-43), so deleting setPaperSize/setOrientation at lines 124-125 leaves every other test (lines 82-86, 107-112, 130-144) passing. Since handleSubmit writes paperSize/orientation to setPageSetup (lines 154-163), the undetected defect would silently rewrite an A4/landscape document to Letter/portrait on Apply — a user-visible, data-affecting change, matching the major bar for vacuous coverage under the test-adequacy lens.
